**Two quick moves of a flow leave waiting runs in the wrong queue** · minor

**What happens:** the DB ends on one group, but the waiting jobs taken by the other call stay in that call's queue.

**Why (code path):**
- `flow-worker-group.service.ts:90-103` reads `previousGroupId`, updates, then migrates, with no lock or conditional update
- two calls both read the same old group and both migrate from it

Main has the same race for projects.

**Repro:** on an unpinned flow with waiting runs, send in parallel:
`POST /v1/worker-groups/flows/<id>` `{"workerGroupId":"A"}`
`POST /v1/worker-groups/flows/<id>` `{"workerGroupId":"B"}`
→ flow.workerGroupId is one of them; part of its jobs sit in the other's queue

**Fix:** `UPDATE … RETURNING` the old value under a per-flow lock.

**Project update saves other fields, then returns 400** · minor

**What happens:** a request with a bad worker group name answers 400, but the other fields were already saved.

**Why (code path):**
- `platform-project-service.ts:134-191`: the transaction commits first
- → `:197-203` `assignProjectToGroup` runs outside it and throws VALIDATION for `''`, `__none__` or a wrong-scope label
- main wrote `workerGroupId` inside the transaction, with no validation

**Repro:**
`POST /v1/projects/<id>` `{"displayName":"renamed","workerGroupId":""}` → 400
`GET /v1/projects/<id>` → displayName is "renamed"

**Fix:** validate the label before the transaction.

**Group names with `:` break the queue and leak Redis connections** · minor (major on cloud) · cloud + self-hosted

**What happens:** a flow pinned to `a:b` can never enqueue, and every webhook for it leaks one Redis connection. Webhooks are public, so a flood can exhaust the shared Redis.

**Why (code path):**
- `worker-group-queues.ts:34-35` accepts `a:b`
- with no worker online for it, the scope list is `[]`, so the assignment is accepted
- → every webhook: `job-queue.ts:30` → `ensureQueueExists:163` runs `await redisConnections.create()` before `new Queue(...)`
- → BullMQ 5.61 throws "Queue name cannot contain :" (`queue-base.js:35`)
- the ioredis client already connected (no `lazyConnect` in `redis-options.ts`) and is never closed

Main already allows this for projects.

**Repro:**
```ts
expect(workerGroupQueues.isRoutableWorkerGroupId('a:b')).toBe(false) // fails today
```
`POST /v1/worker-groups/flows/<id>` `{"workerGroupId":"a:b"}` → 200, then call the flow's webhook → enqueue throws, connection stays open

**Fix:** require `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/` in `isRoutableWorkerGroupId`.

issue.body:
## Description

Server side of the self-serve Enterprise trial: a platform admin on Free, Free legacy, Plus or Team can start a 7-day, no-card trial of every Enterprise feature from a locked feature. The trial is granted by the billing console as a $0 add-on next to the platform's current plan, so the base plan and its AI credits stay as they are. It is offered on Cloud and on self-hosted Enterprise edition; Community has no billing code and gets 404s. In code the feature is the **self-serve trial**; screens and emails keep calling it the Enterprise trial, and the Autumn add-on id is `self_serve_trial` (`PlanName.SELF_SERVE_TRIAL`). The console and the Autumn plan must be renamed from `enterprise_trial` before release, or AP finds no trial.

- **Routes (platform admins only):** `GET /v1/platform-billing/self-serve-trial` returns the trial status, and `POST /v1/platform-billing/self-serve-trial/start` starts it. Only the start calls the console, which tells Cloud from self-hosted by the credential AP sends and takes the owner email from the platform's billing customer; the browser sends neither.
- **Who can start it:** only platforms on `free`, `free_legacy`, `plus`, `plus_annual`, `team` or `team_annual`. Everyone else (AppSumo, Plus chat, Enterprise, custom deals) gets the new `ineligible` state, so no screen offers the trial, and a start is refused without calling the console. The console checks the plan too and answers 403, which AP reads as `ineligible`.
- **No trial dates in the database:** AP reads the dates at each entitlements refresh from Autumn's subscription list (`customers.listSubscriptions`, active and expired rows of the trial plan; the newest start wins, and an expired trial ends at its `expiresAt`, or else at its `trialEndsAt`) into a Redis cache (`platform_plan:self-serve-trial:v2:<platformId>`, 24 hours). A refresh that finds no trial never clears a cached one, so a lagging Autumn read right after a start cannot hide it. Hot paths only read the cache; the admin status route reads Autumn once on a miss.
- **Nothing about the trial in the database:** an owner who already used the trial on another platform is still offered it there. The console refuses the start, the dialog says the trial was already used, and nothing is remembered, so the offer shows again on a later visit. The console's check is what stops a second trial.
- **Members:** `GET` and `POST /v1/platforms/:id` return `selfServeTrial: { startedAt, endsAt }` while a platform has had a trial, for signed-in non-embedded users, so the countdown shows for everyone.
- **During the trial:** a successful start keeps its dates in the cache right away and lets the next plan read refresh again, so a failed or lagging refresh still shows the running trial. A seat reduction scheduled on the base plan doesn't cap invites while the trial runs.
- **Trial end:** once the end date passes, AP stops granting the trial's features, seats and team projects, even if Autumn still lists the add-on as active.
- **Activepieces AI during the trial:** a plan with Embedding hides the Activepieces AI provider, and the trial grants Embedding. The provider now shows whenever the plan carries a self-serve trial. That means the trial is running, or it has ended but the plan hasn't been refreshed since, so its Embedding is still the trial's. The check reads the trial dates from the cache and asks Autumn only when the cache is empty. If Autumn fails, main's rule applies (Embedding hides the provider). Nothing is stored on the plan, so there is no migration. The Embedding page tells trialers that plans with Embedding don't usually come with the Activepieces AI provider, and that they get both together only during the trial.
- **Telemetry:** `trial.started` when a trial actually starts, and `trial.ended` from the refresh within 30 days of the end, sent once.
- **Billing info:** `GET /v1/platform-billing/info` renames `billingPortalAvailable` to `hasPaymentMethod` (true when the Autumn customer has a payment method). Only the web app reads this field, and its 3 lines change here. The billing overview cache key moves to `v3` because the cached shape changed.
- **Shared:** `@activepieces/shared` 0.211.0 (one bump for the whole stack) adds the trial status types (with `ineligible`), `SELF_SERVE_TRIAL_PLANS` and `selfServeTrial` on the platform response.
- **Brain:** decision 000049 records the design and what is parked for later.

The UI is in #16199, stacked on this PR; the seat grace after the trial is in #16205.

Companion console change: activepieces/console#56.

**Security impact:** these routes turn on Enterprise features for 7 days, so who can start a trial matters.
- The routes are restricted to platform admins, and only platforms on the self-serve plans above are offered or allowed a trial.
- Neither the browser nor AP sends the owner email or the edition. The console takes the email from the platform's billing customer and the edition from the credential.
- On Cloud, AP authenticates to the console with the console secret, which only AP Cloud holds. A self-hosted instance can only act for its own billing customer.
- The console enforces the rest: the plan, one trial per owner and edition, plus its own access checks.

## How was this tested?

- **End-to-end on the trial box** (Cloud and EE) with the console, the Autumn sandbox and a mail catcher:
  - A Free platform is offered the trial and starts it; the dates are Autumn's own and are saved on the customer; members see them on the platform.
  - An AppSumo platform reads `ineligible` and gets no "Start free trial" anywhere; AP refuses the start and the console answers 403.
  - After the console ended the trial, AP read the end from the customer; the ended state, dialog and seat grace (#16205) followed.
  - A self-hosted EE platform started its trial with its billing key, from the UI, for an owner who had already used the trial on Cloud.
  - Free legacy (comped through the console) is offered the trial and starts it; on the second platform of an owner who already used it, the start is refused with the already-used dialog and the offer comes back after a reload; a repeat start on an ended trial never calls the console.
- The Activepieces AI rule and the Embedding page note are covered by API and unit tests, `tsc` and lint; they were not run on the box.
- `tsc` (api, web) passes and eslint has 0 errors on the changed files.

- [x] Unit tests for the status in each state (eligible, active, ended, ineligible per plan), the Autumn read on a cache miss, the start (dates cached, console refusals as `used` or `ineligible`, a failed refresh), the console call per edition (only the customer id; 409 and 403 without an error log), and the refresh (dates from the add-on or the customer, a refresh finding nothing never clears saved dates, `trial.ended` only within 30 days). API tests: admin only, CE 404, ineligible plans never reach the console, one start, a start the console refuses answered as used and asked again next time, and `selfServeTrial` on the platform for members. Activepieces AI: API tests for a plan without Embedding, Embedding without a trial, a running trial, an ended trial before and after the plan is refreshed, and a platform without an Autumn customer; unit tests for the cache, one Autumn read on a miss, an Autumn failure and a platform without an Autumn customer. Full suites at the top of the stack (#16205, which includes this PR's code) before the last rebase: unit 1635, Cloud 807, EE 553, CE 1524 and web 1572. After rebasing on main: unit 1648 (the 2 Redis files run against a local Redis) and web 1729 at the top of the stack, and at this PR the related unit (104), Cloud (65), EE (42) and CE (32) tests passed, plus `tsc` (api, web) and lint with 0 errors.

issue.body:
## Description

Stacked on #16199 (the trial UI design pass, on top of #16017). When a self-serve Enterprise trial ends with more users than the base plan's seats, the platform gets a **7-day grace** instead of a blocking dialog. When the grace ends, the users added during the trial who fall outside the plan's seats are deactivated automatically. Decision 000049 records the rule.

**What people see**
- Every member sees "Enterprise trial ended · N days left" in the sidebar, where the trial countdown was. The tooltip says users added during the trial beyond the plan's seats lose access on that date unless an admin upgrades.
- Admins also get a notice and a **Manage seats** button in the one-time trial-ended dialog ("3 users added during the trial are over the Free plan's seats and will be deactivated on Oct 26"), and an "Enterprise trial ended / Extra users lose access Oct 26" row in the platform admin sidebar. For admins, the sidebar line opens Manage seats too.
- Manage seats is the existing "Deactivate users" dialog, now closable, with the users who would leave already ticked and labelled "Leaves {date}". Admins can change who goes, deactivate now, or upgrade.
- At the deadline, the users added during the trial beyond the plan's seats are deactivated, newest first, whatever their role. Users from before the trial, users who joined after it ended and the owner are never removed, and nothing is deleted. A removed user sees "User has been deactivated" when signing in, now also on the email-code path, which used to show a generic error.
- Platforms that fit their plan when the trial ends see nothing new. The console's trial-ended email now says that extra users added during the trial are deactivated 7 days later unless the platform upgrades.

**How**
- **Nothing about the grace is stored.** The deadline is the first daily run (15:30 UTC) at or after the trial end plus 7 days, worked out from the trial's dates (#16017 keeps them in a cache, read from Autumn). The grace shows only while the platform is over its seats and billing is not known to be off for its plan.
- `trial-seat-grace.ts` owns the rule. It counts active users, embedded ones included, plus seat-holding invites against the plan's current `usersLimit`, and picks the newest users created while the trial ran, never the owner. A downgrade scheduled during the grace does not lower that number; its cap still blocks new invites and reactivations.
- Members get the deadline as `selfServeTrial.seatGraceEndsAt` on `GET /v1/platforms/:id`. `GET /v1/platform-billing/info` returns `seatGrace: { usedSeats, seatLimit, userIds }`, worked out on each read, which the dialog uses as its target and to pre-tick.
- A daily system job, `trial-seat-grace-sweep` (15:30 UTC), is scheduled in `licenseKeyUsageReportModule` next to the daily license-key usage report, only on Cloud and EE. It first refreshes from Autumn the platforms on a self-serve plan that still show the trial's unlimited seats, so a platform nobody opened since its trial ended is still caught. It then looks only at platforms with more active users and seat-holding invites than their plan allows (5 on Free), found in one grouped query (about 0.6 seconds on production data), reads their cached trial dates in one Redis call, checks which of them had the trial, and acts once the deadline time has passed, up to 3 days late, so a later change to the plan's seats never deactivates trial users unannounced. It refreshes the plan from Autumn first, so an upgrade during the grace removes nobody. Then it locks the plan row, the platform's active users and its seat-holding invites, recounts and deactivates in one transaction, so a concurrent admin change cannot make it remove too many, and sends `trial.seats.deactivated` with the count. If a platform fails, the others still run, then the run fails and the job retries every hour, up to 6 attempts.
- `DeactivateUsersDialog` loses its blocking `enforced` mode and gains `preselectedUserIds`, `preselectedLabel`, `description` and `actions`. It lists users and platform invitations, as on main. If its user or invite list fails to load, it shows the fetch error with a retry instead of empty rows, and Manage seats does the same when the billing info fails to load.
- Also in this PR:
  - partial-failure handling in the dialog
  - one plan refresh on the first day after a trial ends, run from the trial-ended dialog, so its features switch off promptly
- Embedded users count as seats everywhere, as on main: the grace count reuses main's `countUsedSeats`, the sweep's grouped query counts the same users, and there is no `excludeEmbedded` filter on the users list. An embedded user keeps access while their token is valid, so leaving them out let the grace disagree with billing.
- The trial UI file split and hiding the Cloud "Trial Keys" section during a trial moved to #16199.
- No shared bump of its own: 0.211.0 in #16017 covers the stack.

Note for reviewers: the Free plan's seat count comes from Autumn, so nothing in code changes when it moves. Production grants 5; the Autumn sandbox still grants 1.

## How was this tested?

- Cloud integration tests, `trial-seat-grace.test.ts` (23):
  - The grace runs only after the trial ended and while users added during it are over the plan's seats; it stops showing once the platform fits.
  - Embedded users count like any other user and can be picked; the newest trial users are picked, never the owner, and never users who joined after the trial ended.
  - The grace counts against the plan's current seats, not a scheduled downgrade's cap.
  - The job deactivates at the deadline, recounts and removes only the users still over the plan, does nothing after an upgrade or without billing enforced, and leaves a deadline that has not come, or is more than 3 days past, alone.
  - The job skips a platform over its seats that never had a trial without calling Autumn, reads the trial from Autumn when the cache has nothing, and when one platform fails it finishes the others and then fails the run so the job retries.
  - The billing info lists the users for an admin, also without a cached billing state, and members get the deadline on the platform. No grace shows while billing is known not to be enforced.
  - The job waits for the deadline time on the deadline day, refreshes a platform the trial left with unlimited seats and then ends its grace, and counts seats held by pending invites.
  - The job reads the cached trials of every platform over its seats in one Redis call (`distributedStore.getMany`, with its own unit tests).

Full suites before them: unit 1635, Cloud 807, EE 553, CE 1524, web 1572. Manage seats kept the button disabled while the choice left the platform over its seats. The job, run with the trial moved 8 days back, deactivated only the trial member still over the plan and kept the owner and an embedded user (embedded users were left out then; they now count). issue.title: feat(billing): self-serve 7-day Enterprise trial (server)
issue.body:
## Description

Server side of the self-serve Enterprise trial: a platform admin on Free, Free legacy, Plus or Team can start a 7-day, no-card trial of every Enterprise feature from a locked feature. The trial is granted by the billing console as a $0 add-on next to the platform's current plan, so the base plan and its AI credits stay as they are. It is offered on Cloud and on self-hosted Enterprise edition; Community has no billing code and gets 404s. In code the feature is the **self-serve trial**; screens and emails keep calling it the Enterprise trial, and the Autumn add-on id is `self_serve_trial` (`PlanName.SELF_SERVE_TRIAL`). The console and the Autumn plan must be renamed from `enterprise_trial` before release, or AP finds no trial.

- **Routes (platform admins only):** `GET /v1/platform-billing/self-serve-trial` returns the trial status, and `POST /v1/platform-billing/self-serve-trial/start` starts it. Only the start calls the console, which tells Cloud from self-hosted by the credential AP sends and takes the owner email from the platform's billing customer; the browser sends neither.
- **Who can start it:** only platforms on `free`, `free_legacy`, `plus`, `plus_annual`, `team` or `team_annual`. Everyone else (AppSumo, Plus chat, Enterprise, custom deals) gets the new `ineligible` state, so no screen offers the trial, and a start is refused without calling the console. The console checks the plan too and answers 403, which AP reads as `ineligible`.
- **No trial dates in the database:** AP reads the dates at each entitlements refresh from Autumn's subscription list (`customers.listSubscriptions`, active and expired rows of the trial plan; the newest start wins, and an expired trial ends at its `expiresAt`, or else at its `trialEndsAt`) into a Redis cache (`platform_plan:self-serve-trial:v2:<platformId>`, 24 hours). A refresh that finds no trial never clears a cached one, so a lagging Autumn read right after a start cannot hide it. Hot paths only read the cache; the admin status route reads Autumn once on a miss.
- **Nothing about the trial in the database:** an owner who already used the trial on another platform is still offered it there. The console refuses the start, the dialog says the trial was already used, and nothing is remembered, so the offer shows again on a later visit. The console's check is what stops a second trial.
- **Members:** `GET` and `POST /v1/platforms/:id` return `selfServeTrial: { startedAt, endsAt }` while a platform has had a trial, for signed-in non-embedded users, so the countdown shows for everyone.
- **During the trial:** a successful start keeps its dates in the cache right away and lets the next plan read refresh again, so a failed or lagging refresh still shows the running trial. A seat reduction scheduled on the base plan doesn't cap invites while the trial runs.
- **Trial end:** once the end date passes, AP stops granting the trial's features, seats and team projects, even if Autumn still lists the add-on as active.
- **Activepieces AI during the trial:** a plan with Embedding hides the Activepieces AI provider, and the trial grants Embedding. The provider now shows whenever the plan carries a self-serve trial. That means the trial is running, or it has ended but the plan hasn't been refreshed since, so its Embedding is still the trial's. The check reads the trial dates from the cache and asks Autumn only when the cache is empty. If Autumn fails, main's rule applies (Embedding hides the provider). Nothing is stored on the plan, so there is no migration. The Embedding page tells trialers that plans with Embedding don't usually come with the Activepieces AI provider, and that they get both together only during the trial.
- **Telemetry:** `trial.started` when a trial actually starts, and `trial.ended` from the refresh within 30 days of the end, sent once.
- **Billing info:** `GET /v1/platform-billing/info` renames `billingPortalAvailable` to `hasPaymentMethod` (true when the Autumn customer has a payment method). Only the web app reads this field, and its 3 lines change here. The billing overview cache key moves to `v3` because the cached shape changed.
- **Shared:** `@activepieces/shared` 0.211.0 (one bump for the whole stack) adds the trial status types (with `ineligible`), `SELF_SERVE_TRIAL_PLANS` and `selfServeTrial` on the platform response.
- **Brain:** decision 000049 records the design and what is parked for later.

The UI is in #16199, stacked on this PR; the seat grace after the trial is in #16205.

Companion console change: activepieces/console#56.

**Security impact:** these routes turn on Enterprise features for 7 days, so who can start a trial matters.
- The routes are restricted to platform admins, and only platforms on the self-serve plans above are offered or allowed a trial.
- Neither the browser nor AP sends the owner email or the edition. The console takes the email from the platform's billing customer and the edition from the credential.
- On Cloud, AP authenticates to the console with the console secret, which only AP Cloud holds. A self-hosted instance can only act for its own billing customer.
- The console enforces the rest: the plan, one trial per owner and edition, plus its own access checks.

## How was this tested?

- **End-to-end on the trial box** (Cloud and EE) with the console, the Autumn sandbox and a mail catcher:
  - A Free platform is offered the trial and starts it; the dates are Autumn's own and are saved on the customer; members see them on the platform.
  - An AppSumo platform reads `ineligible` and gets no "Start free trial" anywhere; AP refuses the start and the console answers 403.
  - After the console ended the trial, AP read the end from the customer; the ended state, dialog and seat grace (#16205) followed.
  - A self-hosted EE platform started its trial with its billing key, from the UI, for an owner who had already used the trial on Cloud.
  - Free legacy (comped through the console) is offered the trial and starts it; on the second platform of an owner who already used it, the start is refused with the already-used dialog and the offer comes back after a reload; a repeat start on an ended trial never calls the console.
- The Activepieces AI rule and the Embedding page note are covered by API and unit tests, `tsc` and lint; they were not run on the box.
- `tsc` (api, web) passes and eslint has 0 errors on the changed files.

- [x] Unit tests for the status in each state (eligible, active, ended, ineligible per plan), the Autumn read on a cache miss, the start (dates cached, console refusals as `used` or `ineligible`, a failed refresh), the console call per edition (only the customer id; 409 and 403 without an error log), and the refresh (dates from the add-on or the customer, a refresh finding nothing never clears saved dates, `trial.ended` only within 30 days). API tests: admin only, CE 404, ineligible plans never reach the console, one start, a start the console refuses answered as used and asked again next time, and `selfServeTrial` on the platform for members. Activepieces AI: API tests for a plan without Embedding, Embedding without a trial, a running trial, an ended trial before and after the plan is refreshed, and a platform without an Autumn customer; unit tests for the cache, one Autumn read on a miss, an Autumn failure and a platform without an Autumn customer. Full suites at the top of the stack (#16205, which includes this PR's code) before the last rebase: unit 1635, Cloud 807, EE 553, CE 1524 and web 1572. After rebasing on main: unit 1648 (the 2 Redis files run against a local Redis) and web 1729 at the top of the stack, and at this PR the related unit (104), Cloud (65), EE (42) and CE (32) tests passed, plus `tsc` (api, web) and lint with 0 errors.

The web UI for the self-serve 7-day Enterprise plan trial. It sits on top of the trial server work (#16017).

  - **Eligible admins:** the main action is **Start free trial** ("7-day Enterprise plan trial. No credit card."), next to **Explore plans**.
  - **After the trial is used:** a locked click opens **Explore plans** directly.
  - **Members and embedded users:** they are asked to contact an admin.
  - **Community edition:** a link to switching editions and **Talk to sales**.
  - The actions come in two sizes (`LockedActionsSize`), and usage limits use one component (`LockedFeatureUsage`).
- **Start dialog:** what is included, that credits stay the same, a timeline of the trial, and what happens at the end: features pause, nothing is deleted, back on the current plan. Then a short success screen with first steps. If the trial was already used, or the start fails, the dialog says so.
- **Sidebar:** one line in the credits card, "Enterprise trial · 5 days left". On the last day it says "last day". Admins can click it to go to Billing. On an Enterprise plan without a trial, admins see the plan with **Talk to sales**.
- **Notice** (admins only, top of the page):
  - First 2 days: "You are on a free trial of the Enterprise plan until {date}."
  - The day before the end and the last day: "Your Enterprise plan trial ends tomorrow / today at {time}." It has **Explore plans** and **Talk to sales**, and can be dismissed for the day.
  - Dismissals are saved per platform, user and trial end date.
- **After the trial ends** (admins): one dialog, shown once within 14 days of the end: "Thanks for trying the Enterprise plan. It ended on {date}. You are back on {plan}." It lists what is still there (flows, connections, data, credits) and what is locked for changes, with **Explore plans** and **Talk to sales**.
- **Billing:** the current plan card shows the trial while it runs ("N days left", when it ends, "After that, you are back on {plan}."), and offers the trial when the platform can start it. The plan name is Autumn's own plan name.
- **Embedding page:** during a trial, it says that plans with Embedding don't usually include the Activepieces AI provider.
- **License keys:** the Cloud "Trial Keys" section is hidden while a trial runs.

**How it reads the trial**
- **Platform first:** every user reads the trial dates from the platform (`platform.selfServeTrial`). Admin-only screens also read `/v1/platform-billing/info`. There is no client timer; dates are worked out when a screen renders.

- **Texts:** ICU messages handle today, tomorrow and later dates in one string, so each text has one translation key.

- **Start dialog:** what is included, that credits stay the same, a timeline of the trial, and what happens at the end: features pause, nothing is deleted, back on the current plan. Then a short success screen with first steps. If the trial was already used, or the start fails, the dialog says so.
- **Sidebar:** one line in the credits card, "Enterprise trial · 5 days left". On the last day it says "last day". Admins can click it to go to Billing. On an Enterprise plan without a trial, admins see the plan with **Talk to sales**.
- **Notice** (admins only, top of the page):
  - First 2 days: "You are on a free trial of the Enterprise plan until {date}."
  - The day before the end and the last day: "Your Enterprise plan trial ends tomorrow / today at {time}." It has **Explore plans** and **Talk to sales**, and can be dismissed for the day.
  - Dismissals are saved per platform, user and trial end date.
- **After the trial ends** (admins): one dialog, shown once within 14 days of the end: "Thanks for trying the Enterprise plan. It ended on {date}. You are back on {plan}." It lists what is still there (flows, connections, data, credits) and what is locked for changes, with **Explore plans** and **Talk to sales**.
- **Billing:** the current plan card shows the trial while it runs ("N days left", when it ends, "After that, you are back on {plan}."), and offers the trial when the platform can start it. The plan name is Autumn's own plan name.
- **Embedding page:** during a trial, it says that plans with Embedding don't usually include the Activepieces AI provider.
- **License keys:** the Cloud "Trial Keys" section is hidden while a trial runs.

**How it reads the trial**
- **Platform first:** every user reads the trial dates from the platform (`platform.selfServeTrial`). Admin-only screens also read `/v1/platform-billing/info`. There is no client timer; dates are worked out when a screen renders.
- **Telemetry:** "Talk to sales" sends one event, `sales.handoff.clicked`, with the location in the web app. The locked feature link no longer also sends `platform.admin.sales.contacted` (only platform admins see the link, so it added nothing). Property names are unchanged.
- **Texts:** ICU messages handle today, tomorrow and later dates in one string, so each text has one translation key.
